cells.speakerNotes: 0:00. No title slide. Read the question and let the room count. Do not name any tool yet.

Reveal: four. Container image, service image, cross-repo checkout ref, pre-commit rev. If someone says five, they found runs-on: ubuntu-latest, which is also mutable and which no tool pins. Credit them.
The second question is what Part 2 answers. Leave it hanging.
0:03. Fifteen seconds. Name only; the motivation follows the 87.8% data slide.
Thirty seconds. The room already agrees. Do not belabor it.
One incident, one slide, primary sources only. If task 9 is not done, cut this slide.

Scope the claim exactly as written on the slide. One in eight in-scope repositories is fully pinned. Keep this figure apart from the one-in-seven figure that comes next. Bridge: 'Most of you have not done step one. This talk is about what remains after step one.'

Forty-five seconds. Date the story: zizmor now ships an unsafe-tier --fix for unpinned-uses, so say 'the tools I knew in August 2026'. The date comes from the project's public first commit. Do not name the employer, the repository count, or the trigger; none is cleared. Credit ratchet and pinact by name; the point is the list, not the tool. Do not name pinref here. This leads into the reference inventory.
0:07. Coverage boundary: the usual pinning advice focuses on uses:. Other references still execute code. Save the platform controls for Part 3.
Forty-five seconds total, not per row. Point at the right-hand column. Pre-commit is the row the demo uses.
Forty-five seconds. The title in one slide: pinned, and still not pinned. Do not quote a number; the scan did not measure transitive references.
Methodology before the number, so nobody has to ask. Mention the 100-star floor here and again on the deflating slide.
The centerpiece. Pause after the number.
The container image is the largest single component. Call out the separate pre-commit denominator before anyone else does.
Volunteer the inverse before a hostile questioner computes it. Do not call the rest clean.
Twenty seconds. Self-implicating detail; it buys credibility for the tool table that follows.
Neutral framing. ratchet is near-complete on GitHub Actions; say so. The disclosure is on the slide; read it.

Forty-five seconds. The measurement is GitHub-only; this slide is from vendor documentation, so say 'the docs say', not 'I measured'. Point at the CircleCI line: the platform that solved the config layer still runs a mutable image. Impostor commits beyond GitHub are on a backup slide.
0:17. A fixed SHA answers 'which content?', not 'whose commit?'. The lockfile is one available answer for actions, not the premise of this section.
Quote GitHub's own docs; this is documented behavior, not a discovery. The contribution is showing what the one sentence means in practice.
Live only if the network cooperates; cut to the recording without apologizing. Prefer the pre-commit variant: one demo carries both halves of the talk.
Ask the room what they would have caught. Nobody catches it; that is the point.
Claim only behavior observed in task 7. Keep the qualified wording: 'tools I reviewed'.

Say the limitation out loud. A lockfile can verify action origin at run time, but it does not cover pre-commit revs or cross-repo checkout refs. Audit those separately. This brings the provenance demo back to the measured surface without implying that no other provenance checker exists.
0:23. Shift from what is exposed to what it costs to fix.

One minute. Recommend all three before any third-party tool. Explain that the preview lockfile covers transitive action dependencies, not image bases, pre-commit hooks, or checkout refs. Immutable releases are a publisher control: you cannot require them of the actions you consume. Re-verify all three in March 2027.
Replace <digest> only with a digest resolved during rehearsal; never invent one.
Anticipates the 'digest pins miss security patches' question. The answer is pin plus automated updates, with a deliberate cooldown.
Fill from the public-corpus dry run only. If task 17 is not done, cut this slide; use the time for the review-diff beat in Part 2. Do not imply internal rollout results.
Callback to the motivation: the detectors I knew could report the problem, but the task needed a bulk fixer. These are complementary layers, not competitors.
Thirty seconds. Leave it up long enough to photograph. These commands were tested on a fixture on 2026-10-25; re-run them before the talk.
0:33. The slide people photograph. Leave it up for a beat.
Twenty seconds. One URL matters: the published scanner and data.
0:35. Ten minutes of questions. Backup slides follow.
Backup for 'Can impostor commits happen outside GitHub?'. GitLab findings come from source review; say 'the source says'. The Bitbucket line is from Atlassian documentation.
Backup for 'Your pre-commit number has a small denominator'.
